title: VUA packages-ops result v0.1
description: Result documents for the packages-ops v0.1 write face slice A1 = removal (proposal 026 freeze batch 2026-09-19). Envelope mirrors the standing wire shape (schemaVersion/operation/result, same as project-inspection and project-ops); the envelope const is the word-list-row family version 0.1 and the result document carries its own family const vua.packages-ops/v0.1 — the two versions are independent (the c914cf2 standing rule: every wire row cites a version constant of its own). Operation/kind lock: packages.previewRemove is a synchronous query and answers kind=plan exactly (its failures are wire-envelope errors, not result arms); packages.applyRemove is a nine-state task whose terminal reflux answers kind=receipt or kind=rejected. kind=plan: the confirmation-face projection of the port's ChangePreviewV1 — every change the removal would make (items with kind/version/reason), the conflict warnings (conflicts, free-text machine reasons — the confirm UI must warn), the legacy-files/folders cleanups the removal would sweep (removeLegacyFiles/removeLegacyFolders), the destructive boolean (true when conflicts or legacy removals exist, ADR-0006), and the digest the apply phase must confirm (FNV-1a over the canonical item list). kind=receipt: the AUDIT receipt frozen per the core ruling (change list + actual result, proposal-014 import receipt precedent) — the confirmed digest echoed back, the explicitly requested package ids, and the actually removed change items the backend reports (port apply_remove {removed: items} verbatim); task correlation lives on the task surface (taskId/revision), this document is a reflux payload, not a persisted link. kind=rejected: a typed guard refusal evaluated INSIDE the task; the guard closed set is frozen here and codes follow the vua.packages.* snake-case family (first freeze batch of the family — closed set stands as written, guard value = code suffix). additionalProperties:false everywhere is the false-assertion guard: facts with no port carrier (post-removal re-inspection, byte counts, timestamps, update faces) are INVALID by schema, not merely discouraged.

packageId.description: The VPM package identifier (the manifest name). No tighter pattern is frozen: the word list transports facts, it does not re-litigate upstream id grammar.

version.description: Target version for installs; null for removals (port fact: Option, verbatim).

reason.description: Machine reason, e.g. transitive_dependency, conflict; null when the backend carries none (port fact: Option, verbatim — never padded).

items.description: Every change the removal would make (transitive dependency removals among them, ORC-WF-002: the plan must cover every change the backend will make).

conflicts.description: Free-text machine reasons for dependency breakage the removal would cause — the transparency face; the confirm UI must warn, the authoritative verdict stays server-side.

destructive.description: True when the change set contains conflicts or legacy removals (ADR-0006) — the confirm UI must warn; a false assertion is checkable against the other four faces.

digest.description: FNV-1a over the canonical item list; the applyRemove confirmedDigest binds to exactly this value.

confirmedDigest.description: The digest the user confirmed, echoed — the audit link between the confirmation face and the executed result.

requestedPackageIds.description: The explicit request list, verbatim — the change list half of the audit receipt.

removedItems.description: What the backend actually removed (port apply_remove {removed: items} verbatim) — the actual-result half of the audit receipt.
